request.user:
[2024 fall ms math-stat — problem 2]

Single observation $Y$ with density $f(y\mid\theta) = (\theta+1)y^\theta$, $0<y<1$. Test $H_0: \theta = 0$ vs $H_a: \theta > 0$ at level $\alpha$. (1) Show a UMP test exists, find it, and give its exact form in terms of $\alpha$. (2) Give its power function in terms of $\alpha$.

response.text:
Let \(0<\alpha<1\). The density is

\[
f(y\mid \theta)=(\theta+1)y^\theta,\qquad 0<y<1,
\]

with \(\theta>-1\). We test

\[
H_0:\theta=0 \qquad \text{vs.}\qquad H_a:\theta>0.
\]

Under \(H_0\), \(Y\sim \operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\).

---

## (1) UMP level \(\alpha\) test

For fixed \(\theta>0\), the likelihood ratio of \(\theta\) versus \(0\) is

\[
\frac{f(y\mid \theta)}{f(y\mid 0)}
=
(\theta+1)y^\theta.
\]

Since \(\theta>0\), this is an increasing function of \(y\) on \((0,1)\). Therefore, by the Neyman–Pearson lemma, the most powerful level \(\alpha\) test of

\[
H_0:\theta=0
\]

against the simple alternative

\[
H_1:\theta=\theta_1>0
\]

rejects for large values of \(Y\).

Because the rejection region has the same form for every \(\theta_1>0\), namely

\[
Y>c,
\]

the same test is most powerful against every simple alternative \(\theta_1>0\). Hence it is UMP for testing \(H_0:\theta=0\) against \(H_a:\theta>0\).

Under \(H_0\), \(Y\sim \operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\), so choose \(c\) such that

\[
P_0(Y>c)=\alpha.
\]

Since \(P_0(Y>c)=1-c\), we get

\[
c=1-\alpha.
\]

Thus the UMP level \(\alpha\) test is

\[
\varphi_\alpha(Y)
=
\begin{cases}
1, & Y>1-\alpha,\\
0, & Y\le 1-\alpha.
\end{cases}
\]

Equivalently, reject \(H_0\) iff

\[
Y>1-\alpha.
\]

Because the distribution is continuous, no randomization is needed. Its size is exactly

\[
P_0(Y>1-\alpha)=\alpha.
\]

---

## (2) Power function

For general \(\theta>-1\), the CDF of \(Y\) is

\[
F_\theta(y)
=
\int_0^y (\theta+1)t^\theta\,dt
=
y^{\theta+1}, \qquad 0<y<1.
\]

Therefore the power function of the test is

\[
\pi(\theta)
=
P_\theta(Y>1-\alpha).
\]

Using the CDF,

\[
\pi(\theta)
=
1-F_\theta(1-\alpha)
=
1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1}.
\]

In particular, under \(H_0\),

\[
\pi(0)=1-(1-\alpha)=\alpha,
\]

so the test has exact level \(\alpha\).

Thus the power function is

\[
\boxed{\pi(\theta)=1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1}}, \qquad \theta>-1,
\]

and on the alternative \(\theta>0\),

\[
\boxed{\pi(\theta)=1-(1-\alpha)^{\theta+1}>\alpha.}
\]
